name: Why is my toilet constantly running?

mainEntity.name: Why is my toilet constantly running?

acceptedAnswer.text: A running toilet is typically caused by a faulty flapper valve that no longer seals properly, allowing water to continuously leak from the tank into the bowl. Other common issues include an improperly adjusted or broken fill valve, a float that is set too high (causing water to overflow into the overflow tube), or a worn-out flush handle mechanism. These problems lead to wasted water and higher utility bills.
acceptedAnswer.description: A constantly running toilet is usually due to a faulty flapper valve, a misadjusted fill valve, or an incorrect float height, leading to water waste.
